items.title: Man Convicted in $24M Crypto Ponzi Scheme
points: A defendant was found guilty of running a Ponzi scheme (investment scam where early investors are paid returns using new investor funds rather than genuine profits) that defrauded victims of $24 million in cryptocurrency.
The conviction demonstrates regulators and law enforcement are actively prosecuting large-scale crypto fraud cases.
This case reflects ongoing concerns about fraudulent schemes targeting crypto investors who may lack traditional financial protections.

items.title: Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Go Live on Base
points: Coinbase launched tokenized stocks (NVDAc, METAc, AAPLc, GOOGLc) on Base blockchain, entering a $2.48B tokenized public equities market currently led by Ondo at $872.7M market share.
Four tokenized equities launched under the B20 standard with underlying shares held 1:1 by Alpaca under Abu Dhabi Global Market supervision, restricted to non-US eligible jurisdictions.

Day-one metrics: $4.55M combined onchain value, $3.06M in DEX (decentralized exchange, a platform for trading crypto without a central intermediary) liquidity, and $10.8M in 24-hour trading volume across roughly 50 integrated protocols including Aave, Morpho, Aerodrome, 0x, and 1inch.
Dividends and stock splits settle via an onchain multiplier that keeps position balances static, preventing disruption to DeFi (decentralized finance) collateral positions.
Agentic trading integrations are already underway through Virtuals and Treasures platforms.

items.title: AI Agents as Crypto's Next Billion Users
points: AI agents are emerging as a distinct crypto user cohort, autonomously spending stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to stable assets like the US dollar) to pay for services without human approval.
The trend is described as crypto's "Napster/LimeWire era" of agentic payments, referencing early, chaotic peer-to-peer file-sharing services.
Coinbase is targeting machine-initiated transactions that operate outside traditional user onboarding, viewing stablecoin micropayments as a structural (not cyclical) demand driver.
Infrastructure and protocols that capture agent wallet share now could define the settlement layer for future machine-to-machine commerce.

items.title: Elysium L2 Aims to Fix Hyperliquid's Throughput Constraints
points: Kinetiq launched Elysium, a new Layer 2 blockchain (a secondary network built on top of a main blockchain to increase speed and reduce costs), to solve Hyperliquid's throughput bottlenecks.
Elysium reduces transaction costs from about $20 to near-zero and uses HYPE as its gas token instead of USDC.

It targets block time parity with HyperCore and includes an L1Read precompile giving PropAMMs (proprietary automated market makers, systems that automatically price and trade assets) top-of-block oracle price freshness for tighter quotes.
A native token generation platform creates a path from early-stage AMM bootstrapping through Elysium integration, HyperCore spot listing, and eventual HIP-3 perpetual futures listing.
Sequencer fees are split 50% toward programmatic KNTQ token purchases (burned to the Hyperliquid Assistance Fund), with the remainder split between builders and the Kinetiq treasury.

items.title: EntropyIO Opens Private Company Exposure Markets on Hyperliquid
points: EntropyIO launched the first liquid perpetual markets (derivative contracts with no expiry date) for gaining price exposure to private companies on Hyperliquid.
Anthropic is the first underlying asset offered on the platform.

items.title: Stablecoin Lending Landscape on Solana
points: Three platforms control about 92% of Solana's tracked stablecoin lending TVL (total value locked, the amount of assets deposited in a protocol): Kamino, Jupiter Lend, and Loopscale.
Kamino uses a shared pool architecture with 15 audits and 4 formal verifications, and has had zero exploits since its 2023 launch; it isolates riskier collateral into separate markets.
Jupiter Lend combines earning and borrowing through a single Liquidity Layer with dynamic withdrawal ceilings that throttle liquidity-shock risk.

Loopscale offers a Credit Order Book with fixed rates and durations for rate certainty, but suffered a $5.8M price feed exploit in April 2025 that was fully recovered within 48 hours via a 10% bounty payment to the attacker.
Platform choice maps to different needs: variable-rate liquidity depth (Kamino), combined earn-and-borrow with shock controls (Jupiter), or predictable fixed rates with thinner markets (Loopscale).
